The scar at a shoreline — rendered offline from real terrain

Scenario demo-highyield-nuke, cells 59,38 to 85,64, ground zero 64,64, AtomicHighYield bands. Terrain comes from the scenario's own map.bin; the scar placement, the AcceptsSmudgeType gate and the ShoreAlphaAt ramp are the engine's, reproduced line for line. No game was launched.

The ground art is not the tileset. Cells are drawn with real clear1.tem or w1.tem, so Rock, Cliffs and Beach appear as clear ground — the extracted tile cache carries no rock or sand templates. What is exact here is which cells take a scar and at what strength. Read the alpha panels for the mechanism.

1  The fade field — this is the artefact, on its own

White is a cell drawn at full strength, grey is a cell held below it, blue is a cell that takes no scar at all. Nothing here is art: it is ShoreAlphaAt evaluated over the real terrain.

Today — Chebyshev, ramp from 1/3

Three flat steps, and the contours are literal squares because Chebyshev distance makes them so. The ford is held at 1/3 across its whole width.

Proposed — Euclidean, floor 0.7

The shoreline cell stays clearly scarred, and the contour follows the water instead of boxing it.
